items.stem: Explain what is wrong with this sentence and correct it: ‘When Zara met Ines, she was nervous.’
items.answer: Ambiguous pronoun reference: it is unclear who ‘she’ refers to. Corrected: Zara was nervous when she met Ines.
items.markingKey: Award up to 1 mark, 1 for each of the following up to the maximum: identifies the problem (ambiguous pronoun reference); explains it; an accurate correction.

items.stem: Explain what is wrong with this sentence and correct it: ‘The new rules will effect everyone who rides a scooter.’
items.answer: Wrong word (malapropism): ‘effect’ (noun) is confused with ‘affect’ (verb). Corrected: The new rules will affect everyone who rides a scooter.
items.markingKey: Award up to 2 marks, 1 for each of the following up to the maximum: identifies the problem (wrong word (malapropism)); explains it; an accurate correction.

items.stem: Write two contrasting openings (one or two sentences each) for a letter to your local mayor giving your views on volunteering abroad during a gap year: one using a startling statistic and one using an opening in medias res (in the middle of the action). Then explain which is more effective for the audience.
items.answer: Two openings, using startling statistic and in medias res accurately, and a justified evaluation.
items.markingKey: Award up to 2 marks, 1 per valid point: opening using startling statistic; opening using in medias res; both suited to the form; evaluation linked to audience; accuracy.
